title: Gemini is becoming the default AI everywhere you look, whether you like it or not
content:
On September 4, 2026, Google begins the phased shutdown of the voice assistant that defined the last decade of Android.
Google Assistant disappears from mobile devices, Wear OS watches, plus compatible headphones, and the replacement isn't optional. That forced march is the whole strategy in miniature.
In August 2026, the standalone Gemini app crossed one billion monthly active users, a figure that counts the dedicated app and not the billions of people bumping into AI Overviews in ordinary web search.
Plenty of that growth arrived because an operating system changed under people. And benchmark supremacy is a rented crown anyway, passed around every few months.
Distribution is what compounds, so Google is betting convenience beats quality.
The smartphone baseline
Even Siri answers to Gemini
Let's start with the surface you touch a hundred times a day. The corner swipes and long presses that used to summon legacy Assistant now pull up Gemini.
If you want to see the strategy working, look at a Galaxy. Gemini extensions have been turning up inside Samsung's productivity apps, with each One UI build going further.
Even the side button belongs to Gemini out of the box. But hold that thought; there's more.
January 2026 brought a joint statement confirming that Apple's next Foundation Models would be based on Gemini. Siri, of all things, is now downstream of Gemini.
Cars, where you can't switch
The dashboard is Google's now
In April and May 2026, General Motors pushed a free over-the-air update swapping Google Assistant for Gemini across roughly four million eligible vehicles.
Volvo is running the same game. Gemini is shipping in the new Volvo EX60 electric SUV, using the car's cameras to read local parking signs and road markings in real time.
Worth being clear that this is only the embedded half. GM, Volvo, and Polestar are running Google built-in, meaning Android Automotive OS native in the dashboard.
Android Auto is a separate rollout entirely, and Google puts that footprint at more than 250 million compatible vehicles.
TVs and the gadget periphery
Glasses are next
Gemini is becoming the house AI for hardware makers who will never build their own model.
In June 2026, Google rolled out natural language system controls for Gemini on Google TV. It debuted on select TCL sets under a 60-day exclusivity window before opening up to other brands.
Further down the stack, Gemini turns up wherever a manufacturer wants it. For example, Insta360's August 2026 software update for the GO Ultra added a Gemini-backed assistant called Kira for live translation and visual questions.
The same pattern shows up in smart eyewear. XREAL's upcoming project Aura pairs Android XR with Gemini in a glasses form factor.
Gemini spreads across categories because Google sells the whole thing, from wake word to translation to visual recognition, at whatever depth a manufacturer can absorb it.
The antitrust problem
By the time it's illegal, it's habitual
A court order is the only thing that plausibly breaks a compounding distribution advantage. Google lost its search monopoly case.
If the courts decide the same logic applies to AI assistants, that would put pressure on Google's arrangements.
What it wouldn't touch is Android. Google doesn't need permission to make Gemini the assistant on a platform it writes, so the parts of this strategy that compound fastest are the parts sitting furthest from a judge's reach.
And even where the courts can act, they're slow, with appeals in cases this size running for years while the rollout keeps going.
By the time anything binding arrives, Google may already have what it wanted: a few hundred million people who use Gemini out of habit.
What distribution doesn't buy
Consumer defaults on Android don't win corporate cloud contracts, because the two markets are decided differently.
Consumer AI goes to whoever is closest, since most people won't compare models and will use whatever answers when they ask.
Enterprise buying is the opposite. Someone whose job depends on the result running a bake-off before anything is signed, and no amount of pre-installation survives that.
Google's answer to this has been to push Gemini through Workspace, but that's the same distribution play aimed at a different room, and it converts less cleanly when a procurement team is involved.
Google keeps closing the gap, and Antigravity and the newer Flash models show a company that knows exactly where it's behind, but on the serious work that decides these contracts, it's still the challenger.

report.summary: 谷歌将Gemini设为各设备默认AI，强制迁移。
report.background: 2026年9月起，谷歌正式关闭曾主导Android十年的Google Assistant，全面转向Gemini。这一举动是谷歌整体战略的缩影：不依赖模型benchmark的短期领先，而是通过操作系统、车企、电视和眼镜等渠道把Gemini铺到用户触手可及之处。谷歌还拿下了苹果Siri的模型供应，并迅速铺开车载、电视等场景。其背后是典型的‘分发为王’逻辑——即便在反垄断官司缠身、企业云市场仍落后对手的情况下，也先把消费端习惯养成。
key_points: Google Assistant在2026年9月4日从手机、手表和耳机上全面下架，用户被迫改用Gemini，没有回头路。
三星Galaxy的侧键、生产力应用和One UI逐步内嵌Gemini；苹果Siri也基于Gemini，生态边界被彻底打破。
通用、沃尔沃等车企通过OTA把车载助手换成Gemini，超250万辆兼容Android Auto的车也将被覆盖。
谷歌电视、TCL电视、Insta360相机和XREAL眼镜等硬件都接入Gemini，制造商无需自研模型即可获得全套AI能力。
反垄断裁决虽可能限制谷歌的捆绑行为，但诉讼周期漫长，等到判决落地，用户习惯可能已固化。
report.impact: 对AI行业，谷歌用渠道而非纯技术碾压对手，迫使OpenAI等厂商更重视生态合作与终端捆绑。对开发者，Gemini API和Android XR会变成事实标准，但也要警惕单一平台锁定。对普通用户，好处是随处可用、体验统一，坏处是几乎无法避开谷歌的AI，选择权和隐私空间进一步缩小。
report.tools: 开发者可关注Gemini API、Android XR SDK和Google AI Edge套件，车企和硬件厂商可评估Android Automotive OS的Gemini集成方案；想自建场景则可用Gemini Live或Google AI Studio进行原型验证。
